title: Agentic AI Portfolio Assistant (this site)
description: A tool-using AI agent built into this portfolio. Ask it about my work and it calls real tools — searching projects, reading profile data, matching a pasted job description against my actual skills, pulling live GitHub activity — and can scroll the page or open a project for you. It runs as a serverless function with streaming answers, model fallback and rate limiting, so it stays free to run and degrades gracefully to built-in answers.
highlights: Agent loop with six tools: search projects, read profile sections, match a job description against real skills, fetch live GitHub activity, scroll the page, and open a project.
Answers stream over Server-Sent Events and the chat shows each tool call as it runs, with an optional under-the-hood trace of model turns and timings.
Reliability: tries several free Gemini models in order, retries once, time-boxes every attempt, and falls back to a built-in rule-based assistant if the live model is unavailable.
Abuse and cost controls: per-visitor and daily rate limits, input and output size caps, a bounded number of tool rounds, same-origin checks, and the API key stays on the server.
Grounded by design: it is instructed to cite only data returned by its tools, and to treat visitor-supplied text as data rather than instructions.
Covered by browser tests (streaming, page control, offline fallback, formatting) and a CI workflow that runs typecheck, build, tests and a Lighthouse budget on every change.

title: AI Trading Platform
description: A full-stack AI trading platform: a React/TypeScript front end, Python and Node.js APIs, live market and news integrations, and alerts, driven by a multi-agent LLM system on AWS and GCP. A 7-node LangGraph agent logged 3,507 live decisions, and auditing them showed 71.3% were silent API-quota fallbacks.
highlights: Full-stack platform: React/TypeScript front end, Python/Node.js APIs, live market and news integrations, and alerts.
Deployed a 7-node LangGraph agent that logged 3,507 live decisions; auditing them found 71.3% were silent API-quota fallbacks.
Built an evaluation harness where matched placebos erased an apparent +1.71% ten-day return and exposed 82% stated confidence against 45% wins.
The forward audit is written up as a paper (submitted to AIEI 2027), with code, tests and pre-registration materials released on Zenodo.

title: AgriDroneAI: Autonomous Drone Operations Agent
description: A simulation-first, self-operating precision-agriculture drone network. A scheduled GitHub Actions autopilot runs one operating cycle a day, from reading sensors to planning safety-gated missions to auditing the result, with a kill switch and an audit trail. In simulation it kept about 99% of the crop using about 80% less water than a fixed schedule.
highlights: Each daily cycle: read sensors, repair bad data, classify crop stress, plan collision-checked multi-drone missions, safety-gate them, act, retrain on drift, and audit.
Saved about 80% of the water in simulation while keeping about 99% of the crop, versus a fixed schedule.
Honest result: a farmer who simply reacts to the same soil sensors does about as well on yield and profit, so the value shown is automation and coverage, not better agronomy.
8 evaluation and benchmark scripts (stress model, sensor-fault recall, wind, robustness) and 220+ tests behind an 85% coverage gate; daily GitHub Actions cycles open incidents on failure.
PX4/MAVSDK adapter validated in simulation (PX4 SITL), not on real aircraft.

title: Cricket Win Probability and Player Impact
description: A ball-by-ball win-probability engine for men's T20 internationals, built from Cricsheet data. Separate LightGBM models for the first innings and the chase use leakage-safe pre-match Elo ratings, and each ball's change in win probability is credited to players to rate their impact. Served through a FastAPI backend and a React frontend.
highlights: Per-innings LightGBM models with leakage-safe pre-match Elo, tested chronologically on 3,364 T20I matches (2,691 train, 673 test).
Test log loss of 0.554 (first innings) and 0.349 (chase) against a 0.693 coin-flip baseline.
Player impact: every ball's change in win probability is credited to the batter and debited from the bowler, with ratings shrunk toward the role mean.
Served through a FastAPI backend and a React, TypeScript and Recharts frontend.
Documents its own limits: no pitch, bowler-type, field-setting or toss features, and player ratings are directional rather than a ranking.
